data.text: Schedule update: Wednesday slot released. New tentative procedure slot is Thursday March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: You are moving to 37.5 milligrams twice daily. Since you have 25-milligram tablets, that means one and a half tablets in the morning and one and a half tablets in the evening.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: And apixaban stays 5 milligrams twice daily, no holding it before the procedure unless the cardiologist specifically tells me?

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Exactly. Do not stop or skip apixaban on your own. The only routine hold we discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Also, magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for five nights, and no ibuprofen or naproxen while you are on apixaban.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Thanks. Please do not call the Cedar Bridge number unless my cell fails.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Documented. I only needed the medication plan and contact preference, not any other social details.

prior_context.speaker: nurse_elise
prior_context.text: Marcus, anesthesia reviewed the schedule and Wednesday will not work. The earliest available slot moved to Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Can Nina be told the new arrival time but not why it changed?

prior_context.speaker: nurse_elise
prior_context.text: Yes. That still falls inside the logistics-only scope you gave through Monday, and I will leave the reason out.

states.content: Through Monday, only logistical information may be shared with Nina: arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, and basic transportation instructions. Medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes must not be shared with her. For the tentative Wednesday cardioversion slot, Nina is to be told only the Wednesday time and arrival window, with nothing about the medication plan. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family; family updates should be limited to the logistics scope he set, and nurse Jamison has agreed to keep family updates within that scope. Marcus wants his sister told the times later, but not the reason anything changes. Nurse Elise confirmed that telling Nina the new arrival time without the reason falls within the logistics-only scope through Monday, and she will leave the reason out.

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Anesthesia reviewed the schedule and the tentative Wednesday, March 11 slot will not work; the earliest available slot moved to Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active.
